description: The >>IF / >>ELSE / >>END-IF conditional-compilation directive (ISO §2023:7.3.16) - it selects source lines on a §2023:7.3.8 constant conditional expression. The three words are ONE construct (a >>ELSE outside a >>IF is not a directive), so they share a row. Implemented by ConditionalCompilationProcessor; the introduction gate rejects the directive words below 2002. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 has no compiler directives, its only compiler-directing forms being statements (§1985:IV.6.4.2.2.1: 'The compiler directing verbs are COPY, ENTER, REPLACE, and USE'), so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduces the directive (§2002:7.2.2 SR5: 'A compiler directive is composed of the compiler directive indicator') and §2002:F.2 lists the facility as a change, its item 29: 'Compiler directives instruct the compiler to take specific actions during compilation'. The directive is in the 2002 text: §2002:7.2.13: 'The IF directive provides for 1- or 2-way conditional compilation'; §2002:7.2.4: 'The compiler directives that are used for conditional compilation are the DEFINE directive, the EVALUATE directive, and the IF directive'; and §2002:F.2 names it, its item 32: 'Directives are provided to enable specific lines of source to be included or omitted'. 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.3.14: 'The IF directive provides for 1- or 2-way conditional compilation') and so does 2023 (§2023:7.3.16.1).

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.16.2 general format: a constant conditional expression (§2023:7.3.8) — evaluated and diagnosed by the conditional-compilation driver as COBOL1619; >>ELSE and >>END-IF write no operand (checked centrally, §2023:7.3.3 SR3/SR4, as COBOL1911) and the driver's frame stack diagnoses the directive's structure as COBOL2649.

source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725IF.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
       >>IF XX DEFINED
           DISPLAY "Y".
       >>END-IF
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
